name: Compressed hydrogen storage and tube trailers
category: Hydrogen carriers and logistics / compressed gas
principle: Hydrogen is held as high-pressure gas in steel (Type 1) or composite (Type 4) cylinders and moved on tube trailers. Hexagon Purus gives 200 to 250 bar and about 300 to 400 kg for steel trailers, and 350 to 700 bar and 800 to 1,200 kg or more for Type 4 composite trailers.
key_equipment: Type 1 steel and Type 4 composite cylinders

performance.metric: hydrogen per trailer, steel versus Type 4
performance.basis: steel 300 to 400 kg at 200 to 250 bar; Type 4 800 to 1,200 kg or more at 350 to 700 bar; vendor page

source.note: Hexagon Purus, Type 4 cylinders vs traditional steel tube trailers (vendor page)

advantages: Type 4 holds about three times as much hydrogen as steel for the same size (vendor)
limitations: Vendor source only; transport distances limited by cost per kg (not in source)

sources.note: Hexagon Purus, Type 4 cylinders vs traditional steel tube trailers (vendor page)
DOE Hydrogen and Fuel Cells Program Record 20007, Hydrogen Delivery and Dispensing Cost (2020)
DOE Hydrogen and Fuel Cells Program Record 19001, Current Status of Hydrogen Liquefaction Costs (2019)

costs.metric: gaseous tube-trailer delivery and dispensing cost (excluding production)
costs.basis: HDSAM v3.1 early-market levelized delivery plus dispensing, urban market, 1% FCEV penetration, 700 bar dispensing, low-volume component costs; low = 1,000 kg/day station, high = 450 kg/day station; liquid tanker routes cost USD 8.31-11.35/kg in the same comparison; DOE record 19001 notes that at delivery distances above ~400 miles liquid tankers are more cost competitive than gaseous tube trailers

source.note: DOE Hydrogen and Fuel Cells Program Record 20007, Hydrogen Delivery and Dispensing Cost (2020), Table 1 and Table 2
